question_text: A 24-year-old woman with HIV infection comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She has been inconsistently taking combined antiretroviral therapy for the past 5 years. She did not receive any childhood vaccinations because her parents were against them. During the consultation, the patient says that she wants to catch up on the missed vaccinations. Laboratory studies show a CD4+ T lymphocyte cell count of 180/mm3. Administration of the vaccine against which of the following agents should be avoided in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 24-year-old woman with HIV infection comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She has been inconsistently taking combined antiretroviral therapy for the past 5 years. She did not receive any childhood vaccinations because her parents were against them. During the consultation, the patient says that she wants to catch up on the missed vaccinations. Laboratory studies show a CD4+ T lymphocyte cell count of 180/mm3. Administration of the vaccine against which of the following agents should be avoided in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Bordetella pertussis
opb. Human papillomavirus
opc. Haemophilus influenzae
opd. Clostridium tetani
ope. Varicella zoster virus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a patient with severe immunosuppression (CD4+ T lymphocyte count of 180/mm3 due to HIV infection), live vaccines should be avoided to prevent vaccine-related complications. Therefore, administration of the vaccine against Varicella zoster virus (ope) should be avoided in this patient.
